title: A Visitor for the Smile
premise: Hospice nurse Dominic Okafor has always heard the dying count backwards from ten, a private superstition she's never questioned. When every mirror in Blackthorn House begins reflecting the rooms one second late — and something in that delayed reflection starts moving independently of her — she discovers the hospice was built by founders who bound a hungry presence into its walls with an unfinished ritual. The residents' deaths are feeding it, and the final resident, Mr. Aldous Wren, is being pressured to sign papers that will complete the binding and make it permanent. Dominic must reconstruct and finish the founders' interrupted ritual herself, choosing between the loyalty she owes her dying patients and the truth about what she's been keeping alive, before Wren signs on his last night.
about_author: Quentin Vane is the pen name of a former night-shift caregiver who spent six years in residential care facilities across the English Midlands and now writes horror drawn from what the quiet hours actually feel like. Vane lives alone with too many clocks and refuses to own a full-length mirror.

chapters.title: Ten, Nine, Eight
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A routine death watch: Mrs. Halloran counts backwards under her breath as she fades, and Dominic does what she always does — keeps the lights on, checks the doors, writes it off as end-of-life brain activity. But tonight Mrs. Halloran opens her eyes at zero and says, 'It's still here.' Emotional beat: unease planted in the familiar; Dominic's competence as armor against dread.

chapters.title: The Second Behind
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She notices the hallway mirror showing her turning her head a beat after she does. Testing it with deliberate movements, she confirms the lag is real and growing. Night supervisor Priya dismisses it as exhaustion, but the new resident, Mr. Wren, watches Dominic through the lounge glass like he recognizes what's happening to her. Beat: rationality cracking; isolation beginning.

chapters.title: What the Founders Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating Dominic and Wren POVs. Digging in the hospice archive for a maintenance record, Dominic finds the 1911 founding ledger — half a ritual text, pages torn out — and a photograph of the founders standing before a bricked-up doorway. Wren privately admits he came here to die somewhere specific. Beat: the house has a history it hid on purpose; two lonely people circling the same secret.

chapters.title: Counting With Her
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Resident Edith Nwosu begins counting backwards days before any medical reason, and the mirrors show Edith's room empty while Edith sits visibly in the reflection, mouthing numbers. When Dominic touches the glass, the reflected Edith grabs her wrist — cold, grateful, terrified. Beat: horror made intimate; the dead aren't gone, they're held.

chapters.title: Papers of Passage
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. An administrator named Corliss arrives with end-of-life paperwork that reads, on close inspection, like a contract of transfer — Wren's name already inked where a signature belongs. Wren realizes the hospice doesn't host deaths; it harvests them, and he was chosen. He hides the papers. Beat: power revealed as predation; Wren shifts from patient to target.

chapters.title: The Bricked Door
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Following cold air and mirror-lag, she finds the bricked-up doorway behind the laundry — warm to the touch, breathing slowly. Inside the wall, something knocks back when she knocks. Priya catches her there and, shaken, confesses staff have always known the rules: never work alone past three, never let a resident die uncounted. Beat: complicity exposed; the institution is a lid.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Price
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Dominic confronts Priya and learns the truth: finishing the founders' ritual would free the thing but release every held soul — including ones staff loved. Keeping it fed means peace, order, good deaths. Priya begs her to let Wren sign. Dominic must weigh her loyalty to colleagues and residents against the truth that their comfort is built on captivity. Beat: thematic crux; no clean choice.

chapters.title: Zero
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren begins counting backwards involuntarily, and the mirrors now run a full minute late, filled with everyone the house has taken. Corliss corners him with the pen. Dominic arrives mid-signature and tears the page — and the house responds, doors multiplying, lights dying wing by wing. Beat: climax ignites; the ritual's interruption has consequences either way.

chapters.title: The Unfinished Verse
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Armed with the torn ledger pages recovered from inside the wall, Dominic performs the founders' completion in the laundry corridor: not a banishment but a release, spoken aloud while the held souls count down together — ten to one, all of them, in chorus. The brick exhales. The mirrors sync. Beat: climax resolved through the theme — truth chosen over comfortable lies, at real cost.

chapters.title: A Visitor for the Smile
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, weeks later. The hospice is quieter, ordinary, grief now allowed to be just grief; Wren dies naturally, uncounted, smiling at someone only he can see — a visitor, finally welcome. Dominic keeps the lights on out of habit, not fear, and covers the hallway mirror with a cloth she no longer needs. Beat: belonging redefined; peace earned, haunted gently.
